operations.specification: Guest user registration endpoint that creates a temporary guest account with email and password. This operation is associated with the todo_list_users Prisma table. Guests receive initial JWT access and refresh tokens upon registration, enabling them to immediately start using the application without email verification. The registration is open to the public with minimal validation requirements suitable for temporary guest accounts.
operations.name: join
operations.summary: Register a new guest user account in the todo_list_users table.
operations.description:
Creates a new guest user account in the todo_list_users table with email and password credentials. This endpoint is publicly accessible and allows unauthenticated users to register for temporary access to the Todo List application.

The email field must be unique across all users in the todo_list_users table (enforced by unique constraint on email column). The password is securely hashed using bcrypt (minimum cost factor 10) before storage in the password_hash field, ensuring passwords are never stored in plaintext.

Upon successful registration, the API generates initial JWT tokens (access token and refresh token) for immediate use. A corresponding session record is created in the todo_list_sessions table with the current IP address, user agent, and session timing constraints (7-day inactivity timeout and 30-day absolute maximum).

Guest accounts are created with null deleted_at field, indicating an active account. The created_at timestamp is set to the current UTC time and is immutable. The updated_at field is also initialized to the creation timestamp and tracks any subsequent modifications.

Password requirements follow security best practices with bcrypt hashing using cost factor 10 or higher. The email is normalized to lowercase for consistent case-insensitive matching during authentication. No email verification is required for guest accounts - they can use the application immediately upon registration.

This operation must be called before the guest can access any protected todo operations. It is the entry point for new guest users entering the system.

requestBody.description: Guest registration credentials including email and password.

responseBody.description: Guest user account with JWT authentication tokens.

operations.specification: Guest token refresh endpoint that renews expired JWT access tokens using a valid refresh token. This operation is associated with the todo_list_sessions Prisma table for session management. The refresh token is validated for expiration and active session status before issuing a new access token. This enables guests to maintain continuous session access without re-registering.
operations.name: refresh
operations.summary: Refresh expired JWT tokens for a guest user session in the todo_list_sessions table.
operations.description:
Renews JWT access tokens for a guest user by validating the provided refresh token against the session and token management system. This endpoint is publicly accessible for guests with valid refresh tokens obtained from the join operation.

The refresh operation validates that the refresh token exists and is still valid (not expired). The underlying session in the todo_list_sessions table is checked to ensure it remains active (expired_at is null, indicating logout has not occurred) and has not exceeded the absolute timeout threshold (absolute_timeout_at timestamp).

The last_activity_at field in the corresponding todo_list_sessions record is updated to the current timestamp to refresh the 7-day inactivity timeout counter. If the session has been inactive beyond 7 days, the refresh request is rejected and the guest must re-register.

Upon successful refresh, new JWT tokens are generated and returned: a fresh access token with standard expiration (typically 15 minutes) and a refresh token for the next refresh cycle. The old access token becomes invalid and should not be used for subsequent requests.

If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or the associated session has been terminated (expired_at is not null), the refresh fails and the guest must call the join operation again to register a new account and obtain new tokens.

This operation maintains session continuity for active guests without requiring them to re-authenticate. It is essential for keeping guest users logged in across multiple API calls and browser sessions.

requestBody.description: Refresh token from previous authentication response.

responseBody.description: Guest user with renewed JWT authentication tokens.

operations.specification: User registration endpoint that creates a new user account and initializes authentication tokens. This operation handles the complete registration flow for the todo_list_users table, creating a new user record with email and password_hash fields. A corresponding session is created in todo_list_sessions table to track the login context (IP address, user agent, timeout values). The operation generates JWT tokens (access and refresh tokens) that are returned to the client for subsequent authenticated requests.
operations.name: join
operations.summary: Register a new user account in the todo_list_users table and issue initial authentication tokens
operations.description:
This endpoint enables new users to create an account in the Todo List application. It processes registration requests by creating a new record in the todo_list_users table with the provided email address and securely hashed password. The email field must be unique across all users to prevent duplicate accounts; emails are stored in lowercase for case-insensitive matching during login.

The operation validates that the email is not already registered and that the password meets security requirements. Upon successful account creation, the password_hash field is populated with a bcrypt hash (minimum cost factor 10) of the user's password - the plaintext password is never stored in the database. The created_at timestamp is set to the current UTC time, marking the account creation moment, while last_login_at is initialized to null (indicating no login yet) and deleted_at remains null (indicating an active account).

Immediately after user creation, a session record is created in the todo_list_sessions table to represent the initial authenticated session from the registration request. The session stores the client's ip_address and user_agent for device tracking and security monitoring. Session timeout fields are configured: created_at records the registration moment, last_activity_at is set to creation time, expired_at remains null (session is active), and absolute_timeout_at is set to 30 days from creation for maximum session duration enforcement.

The endpoint generates JWT tokens for immediate authenticated access: an access token (short-lived, typically 15 minutes) for API requests and a refresh token (long-lived, typically 7 days) for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication. These tokens encode the user ID and JTI (JWT ID) claim for revocation tracking via the todo_list_token_blacklist table. Tokens are returned in the response for client storage and use in subsequent API requests.

Security considerations include: email uniqueness validation to prevent duplicate accounts, bcrypt password hashing to ensure passwords are never stored plaintext, cryptographically secure token generation to prevent token guessing attacks, and session creation to support multi-device login tracking. Related operations include the login endpoint (POST /auth/user/login) for existing users and the refresh endpoint (POST /auth/user/refresh) for token renewal.

requestBody.description: New user registration credentials including email and password

responseBody.description: Registered user account with issued JWT tokens for authenticated access

operations.specification: User login endpoint that authenticates existing users and generates new authentication tokens. This operation validates the provided email and password against the todo_list_users table record, verifies the password_hash using bcrypt comparison, and returns JWT tokens (access and refresh) for authenticated API access. A new session is created in todo_list_sessions table to represent this login from a specific device, enabling multi-device login support.
operations.name: login
operations.summary: Authenticate a user with email and password, and issue JWT tokens for the todo_list_users table
operations.description:
This endpoint authenticates existing users by validating their email and password credentials. The operation queries the todo_list_users table to locate a user record with the provided email address (emails are stored in lowercase, so the lookup is case-insensitive). Once the user record is found, the provided plaintext password is securely compared against the stored password_hash using bcrypt verification to ensure the password is correct.

Authentication only succeeds if the user account is active (deleted_at is null), preventing login attempts by users whose accounts have been deleted. The last_login_at field in the user record is updated to the current UTC timestamp, recording when this successful authentication occurred. This field is used for tracking user activity and detecting inactive accounts.

Upon successful authentication, a new session record is created in the todo_list_sessions table to represent this login from a specific device or browser. The session captures the client's ip_address and user_agent header, which are stored for device tracking and security monitoring to detect unusual or suspicious login patterns. Session timeout fields are initialized: created_at records the login moment, last_activity_at is set to creation time (updated with each subsequent API request), expired_at remains null (session is active until explicitly logged out), and absolute_timeout_at is set to 30 days from login for enforcing maximum session duration.

The endpoint generates two JWT tokens returned to the client: an access token (short-lived, typically 15 minutes) for making authenticated API requests, and a refresh token (long-lived, typically 7 days) for obtaining new access tokens when the current one expires. Both tokens include the user ID and JTI (JWT ID) claim, with the JTI enabling token revocation tracking through the todo_list_token_blacklist table. The tokens are cryptographically secure and cannot be guessed or forged.

Authentication failure responses (invalid email, incorrect password, or deleted account) do not reveal which condition failed, maintaining user privacy and preventing email enumeration attacks. The response simply indicates "invalid credentials" without distinguishing between missing user or wrong password. Related operations include the registration endpoint (POST /auth/user/join) for new users and the refresh endpoint (POST /auth/user/refresh) for token renewal without re-authentication.

requestBody.description: User login credentials including email and password

responseBody.description: Authenticated user with issued JWT tokens for API access

operations.specification: Token refresh endpoint that renews expired access tokens using a valid refresh token. This operation validates the provided refresh token, verifies it has not been revoked in the todo_list_token_blacklist table, and generates a new access token if validation succeeds. The refresh token lifetime enables users to obtain new access tokens without re-entering their password.
operations.name: refresh
operations.summary: Refresh an expired access token using a valid refresh token for the todo_list_users table
operations.description:
This endpoint implements token refresh functionality, allowing clients to obtain a new access token when their current token expires, without requiring the user to re-enter their password. The operation receives a refresh token from the client, validates it, and generates a new short-lived access token for continued API access.

Token validation includes: (1) verifying the refresh token signature using the configured JWT secret to ensure it has not been tampered with, (2) checking that the token has not expired (the exp claim must be greater than current time), (3) extracting the JTI (JWT ID) claim and user ID from the token payload, and (4) querying the todo_list_token_blacklist table to ensure this token has not been revoked (if the JTI exists in the blacklist, the token is invalid and refresh fails).

The blacklist check prevents token reuse after logout or password change - when users explicitly log out or change their password, all their existing tokens are added to the todo_list_token_blacklist table with revocation_reason documented as 'logout' or 'password_change'. These revoked tokens cannot be refreshed or used for API requests, forcing users to re-authenticate. This implements the security requirement that logging out from all devices invalidates all tokens immediately.

If the refresh token passes all validation checks, a new access token (short-lived, typically 15 minutes) is generated and returned to the client. The new access token encodes the same user ID and includes a new JTI for token tracking. The refresh token itself is not changed or reissued; it continues to be valid until its natural expiration time or until explicitly revoked.

If any validation check fails (invalid signature, expired token, revoked token, malformed payload), the refresh request is rejected and the client must re-authenticate via the login endpoint. Error responses do not reveal which specific validation failed, maintaining security by not leaking information about token state.

The endpoint requires a valid refresh token but does not require an access token, enabling token refresh even when the access token has expired. This allows seamless user experience where the client can obtain new access tokens without manual user intervention. Session activity tracking is also updated if a database session record exists (last_activity_at is set to current time). Related operations include the login endpoint (POST /auth/user/login) for initial authentication and the logout operation (if implemented) for explicit token revocation.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining a new access token

responseBody.description: New access token for continued API access

operations.specification: Password reset request endpoint that initiates the password recovery flow. This operation creates a secure, time-limited token in the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table and sends it to the user's registered email address. The token enables users who have forgotten their password to securely set a new password without needing access to their current credentials.
operations.name: resetPasswordRequest
operations.summary: Initiate password reset flow by generating a time-limited reset token for the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table
operations.description:
This endpoint initiates the password reset process when users forget their password. The operation receives an email address and queries the todo_list_users table to locate the corresponding user account. If a user with the provided email exists and is active (deleted_at is null), a password reset token is created in the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table.

The reset token is a cryptographically secure random value that cannot be guessed or brute-forced. This token is generated using a secure random number generator with sufficient entropy. The token is stored in the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table with the todo_list_user_id foreign key referencing the user requesting the reset. The token field is hashed before storage to prevent token exposure if the database is compromised - plaintext tokens are never persisted.

Token expiration is enforced through the expires_at field, set to 1 hour from creation (created_at + 1 hour). Tokens cannot be used for password reset after this time; if the user's reset link expires, they must request a new token. This time-limited enforcement prevents token reuse attacks where old tokens could be exploited if leaked. The consumed_at field is initialized to null, indicating the token has not yet been used for a password reset.

The reset token is sent to the user's registered email address in a password reset link (e.g., /reset-password?token={token}). The email is sent asynchronously so the API response is not delayed. Users click the link, which delivers them to a frontend form where they can enter a new password and submit it to the password reset confirmation endpoint.

For security, if the provided email does not exist in the todo_list_users table or the account is deleted (deleted_at is not null), the response still indicates success ("Reset link sent if account exists"). This prevents email enumeration attacks where attackers could discover which email addresses are registered in the system. Only the legitimate email recipient receives the actual reset link.

Multiple reset tokens can be generated for the same user if they request multiple resets; each token is independent and valid for 1 hour. When the user later uses one token to reset their password (via the password reset confirmation endpoint), that token is marked as consumed_at, preventing reuse of the same token. Other unexpired tokens for the same user remain valid until their individual expiration times. Related operations include the password reset confirmation endpoint (POST /auth/user/password/reset-confirm) for completing the reset with a token.

requestBody.description: Email address for requesting a password reset token

responseBody.description: Confirmation that reset link was sent (same response for existing and non-existing emails for security)

operations.specification: Password reset confirmation endpoint that completes the password reset flow. This operation validates the provided reset token (checking expiration and consumed status in the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table), updates the user's password_hash in the todo_list_users table, marks the token as consumed, and revokes all existing user sessions/tokens to force re-authentication.
operations.name: resetPasswordConfirm
operations.summary: Complete password reset by validating token and updating password_hash in the todo_list_users table
operations.description:
This endpoint completes the password reset process when users have received and used their password reset link. The operation receives a reset token and new password, then validates the token against the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table to ensure it is legitimate and can be used.

Token validation includes: (1) querying the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table with the provided token to locate the reset request record, (2) verifying the token has not expired by checking that created_at + 1 hour (expires_at field) is greater than current time, (3) ensuring the token has not already been used by checking that consumed_at is null (if consumed_at has a value, the token was already used and cannot be reused for security), and (4) confirming the associated user account exists and is active in the todo_list_users table (deleted_at is null).

If token validation fails for any reason (invalid/not found, expired, already consumed, or user deleted), the reset is rejected with an error response. This prevents attackers from using leaked or old tokens to reset passwords of other users.

Once the token is validated, the user's password is updated. The new password is validated for complexity requirements (minimum length, character variety per security policy), then securely hashed using bcrypt (minimum cost factor 10) and stored in the password_hash field of the todo_list_users table. The plaintext password is never stored or logged. The updated_at field is set to current UTC time, recording when this password change occurred.

After the password is successfully updated, the reset token is marked as consumed by setting the consumed_at field to the current UTC timestamp. This single-use enforcement prevents the same token from being used again to reset the password multiple times. The token record remains in the database for audit trail purposes.

As a security best practice, all existing sessions and tokens for this user are invalidated upon password reset. All active sessions in the todo_list_sessions table for this user are marked as expired (expired_at is set to current time). All tokens that were issued before the password change are added to the todo_list_token_blacklist table with revocation_reason set to 'password_change', ensuring old tokens cannot be used for API requests or token refresh. This forces the user to log in again with their new password, preventing unauthorized access if a token was previously compromised.

The endpoint returns a success response but does not issue new tokens; the user must log in with their new password via the login endpoint to obtain fresh credentials. This ensures the user has successfully proven they own the account (by validating they received the email) and have set a new password. Related operations include the password reset request endpoint (POST /auth/user/password/reset-request) for initiating the reset flow and the login endpoint (POST /auth/user/login) for re-authenticating with the new password.

requestBody.description: Reset token and new password for completing password reset

responseBody.description: Confirmation that password was successfully reset

operations.specification: This operation terminates the current user's active session and invalidates the associated JWT token. When a user explicitly logs out from a device, their current session record in the todo_list_sessions table is marked as expired and the JWT token (identified by JTI claim) is added to the todo_list_token_blacklist to prevent further use. The operation requires the user to be authenticated - the user ID and session information are extracted from the JWT token in the authorization header. Upon successful logout, subsequent requests using the same token will be rejected.
operations.summary: Log out current user from the current device
operations.description:
Terminate the current user's authenticated session and invalidate the JWT token used for this request.

This operation invalidates the session associated with the current device by marking it as expired in the todo_list_sessions table. The JWT token (identified by the jti claim) is added to the todo_list_token_blacklist with revocation reason 'logout' to prevent token reuse. The operation requires an authenticated user - the session and user information are extracted from the JWT token provided in the Authorization header.

Security: Only authenticated users can logout. The revocation is tied to the specific token/session being used, allowing users to maintain other active sessions on different devices. This supports the multi-device login requirement where a user can logout from one device while remaining logged in on others.

After successful logout, the invalidated token cannot be used for any further authenticated requests. The session record is marked with an expired_at timestamp, and the token becomes unusable immediately. This operation should be called as part of the user logout flow before the client discards the token.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful logout

operations.name: logout

operations.specification: This operation terminates all active sessions for the authenticated user across all devices and invalidates all associated JWT tokens. When a user performs a global logout, all session records in the todo_list_sessions table for that user are marked as expired, and all active JWT tokens (identified by their JTI claims) are added to the todo_list_token_blacklist with revocation reason 'global_logout'. This ensures complete invalidation of the user's authentication across all devices. The operation requires the user to be authenticated via JWT token.
operations.summary: Log out current user from all devices
operations.description:
Terminate all of the current user's active sessions across all devices and invalidate all associated JWT tokens.

This operation invalidates all sessions associated with the authenticated user by marking all their session records in the todo_list_sessions table as expired. All active JWT tokens (identified by their jti claims) are added to the todo_list_token_blacklist with revocation reason 'global_logout' to prevent any further use. This is a global logout that affects every device the user is currently logged in from.

Security: Only authenticated users can initiate a global logout. This operation is particularly important for security scenarios such as password changes, suspected account compromise, or when a user wants to ensure no other devices have access to their account. The user must be authenticated to perform this operation, typically as a follow-up action after changing their password.

After successful global logout, all active sessions are terminated and all tokens become unusable. Subsequent requests from any device using previously valid tokens will be rejected. Users must re-authenticate (login) to regain access from any device.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful global logout

Password hash is explicitly excluded from the response for security reasons.
operations.summary: Retrieve the authenticated user's profile information
operations.description:
Get the complete profile of the currently authenticated user. This operation returns all available user account information including email address, account creation and update timestamps, and last login history.

The authenticated user's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT bearer token in the authorization header. Only the authenticated user can access their own profile - there is no ability to view other users' profiles through this endpoint. The user's account must be active (not soft-deleted) to access this endpoint.

Returned information includes email (stored in lowercase), account creation timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601 format), most recent account update timestamp, and the user's last successful login timestamp. The deleted_at field will be null for active accounts, confirming the account has not been soft-deleted. The password_hash field is never included in responses for security reasons.

This operation supports the user's ability to verify their current account information and access profile data for display in user interface settings pages. It is typically called after successful authentication to populate user dashboard or profile screens.

operations.summary: Update the authenticated user's profile information
operations.description:
Update the profile information of the currently authenticated user. This operation allows users to modify their account details such as email address while maintaining account security and data integrity.

The authenticated user's identity is extracted from the JWT bearer token, ensuring that users can only modify their own profile and not other users' accounts. The user's account must be active (not soft-deleted) to perform updates. The request body contains the updated profile information that should be applied to the user's account.

Email address updates must maintain the unique constraint - a new email cannot be the same as any existing user's email in the system. The system will automatically update the updated_at timestamp to reflect when this modification occurred. Password changes are not handled through this endpoint and must use a dedicated password change operation. System-managed fields such as created_at, deleted_at, and last_login_at cannot be modified through this endpoint.

Upon successful update, the operation returns the complete updated user profile with all current account information. This allows the client to immediately reflect the changes in the user interface without requiring a separate profile fetch operation. The password_hash field is excluded from the response for security reasons.

operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of user authentication sessions
operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive list of all authentication sessions belonging to the authenticated user. This operation provides visibility into all devices and browsers from which the user is currently logged in or has recently logged in.

The operation supports advanced filtering options including session status (active sessions with null expired_at vs terminated sessions with set expired_at), creation date ranges, last activity date ranges, and expiration status. Users can identify unusual session activity or manage their login devices by reviewing IP addresses and user agent information associated with each session.

Pagination support allows efficient retrieval of session lists for users with many concurrent sessions. Results can be sorted by creation time, last activity time, or expiration status to help users identify the most recent or most active sessions.

operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information about a specific user authentication session
operations.description:
Fetch complete details about a single authentication session identified by session ID. This operation provides comprehensive session information including device context (IP address and user agent), session timing (creation, last activity, expiration), and current status.

The operation returns all session attributes from the todo_list_sessions table: the unique session identifier, associated user ID, IP address from which the session was established, HTTP user agent string identifying the device/browser, session creation timestamp, most recent activity timestamp, explicit termination timestamp (if logged out), and absolute timeout timestamp (30-day maximum session duration).

Authorization: Only the authenticated user who owns the session can retrieve its details. Attempting to access another user's session returns a 403 Forbidden error. The session ID must correspond to a session owned by the authenticated user.

Security Note: Response provides complete session information including device context (IP address, user agent). User password hash, authentication credentials, and sensitive user account information are not included in any response.

operations.specification: This operation allows authenticated users to verify the validity and integrity of their current JWT token. It validates that the token has not been revoked, has not expired, and still belongs to an active user account. The operation checks the token against the token blacklist table to ensure it hasn't been invalidated through logout or password change. This is a security operation that helps clients determine token state without making other API calls.
operations.summary: Verify the validity of an authenticated user's JWT token
operations.description:
This operation validates the authenticity and current state of a user's JWT authentication token. It performs comprehensive verification including token signature validation, expiration time check, revocation status against the todo_list_token_blacklist table, and confirmation that the referenced user account in the todo_list_users table is still active (deleted_at is null).

The operation requires a valid JWT token to be provided in the Authorization header. The token must contain standard JWT claims including jti (token identifier), sub (user ID), exp (expiration time), and iat (issued time). These claims are validated against system records to ensure token integrity.

Security considerations include verifying that the user account has not been deleted (soft delete marker deleted_at should be null) and confirming the token has not been explicitly revoked in the todo_list_token_blacklist table. The operation implements rate limiting to prevent token verification abuse. The response includes detailed token state information to help clients understand token validity and remaining lifetime.

This operation is commonly used by client applications to preemptively detect expired or revoked tokens before attempting other API calls, enabling graceful token refresh or re-authentication flows. It serves as a validation checkpoint in multi-device authentication scenarios where tokens might be revoked from one device but still active on others.

responseBody.description: Token verification result containing validity status, user information, and token metadata

operations.summary: Terminate a guest user session
operations.description:
This operation terminates an active guest user session in the todo list application. Guest users represent unauthenticated access with limited functionality, typically unable to persist todos permanently. Logout for guests clears their session state and invalidates any guest-specific access tokens or session identifiers.

Unlike authenticated user logout which must revoke tokens in the todo_list_token_blacklist table and update todo_list_sessions records, guest logout performs lightweight session cleanup appropriate for unauthenticated users. The operation may clear browser-stored session identifiers or local state associated with the guest session.

Security considerations for guest logout include properly clearing any client-side storage to prevent reuse of expired guest credentials. Since guests are not tracked in the todo_list_users table (having no persistent account), there is no user account to deactivate or permanent session record to update.

This operation completes the guest user lifecycle and should be called when a guest decides to end their session. It may be followed by either creating a user account (registration) to persist todos, or simply closing the application. The endpoint returns a confirmation message that the guest session has been successfully terminated.

Soft-deleted todos (with non-null deleted_at timestamps) are excluded from results. The operation returns a paginated response containing todo summaries optimized for list display, with option to include full details based on query parameters.

Delete a specific todo item that belongs to the authenticated user. This operation finds the todo by its unique identifier (todoId), verifies that the requesting user owns this todo, and then permanently removes it from the database.

The authenticated user must own the todo for deletion to succeed. If the user attempts to delete a todo created by another user, the system denies access without revealing whether the todo exists (preventing information leakage). If the todo does not exist, the system also returns a not-found error.

Deletion is permanent and irreversible - the todo cannot be recovered after this operation completes. Unlike some systems that implement soft deletes or recovery mechanisms, this todo application permanently removes deleted todos from storage. The system enforces this permanence to keep data clean and storage efficient.

This operation integrates with the todo_list_todos table, which stores all todo items with fields for title, description, completion status, due date, priority, and timestamps. Each todo maintains a user_id foreign key that establishes exclusive ownership - only the user who created the todo (the owner) can view, modify, or delete it. The authentication layer extracts the user ID from the JWT token and uses this to verify ownership before allowing deletion.

operations.summary: Search and retrieve system configuration settings with filtering and pagination
operations.description:
Retrieve system configuration entries from the todo_list_system_config table with advanced filtering, searching, and pagination capabilities. This operation allows querying system-wide settings that control application behavior such as maximum todos per user, feature flags, deployment environment, and security parameters.

The system configuration table maintains operational settings as key-value pairs with additional metadata. Each configuration entry includes: a unique config_key (identifier like 'max_todos_per_user'), the config_value (the actual setting value stored as string), value_type (indicating the data type: string, integer, boolean, or float for proper parsing), a human-readable description, version number for tracking changes, and creation/update timestamps for audit purposes.

This operation supports flexible querying through request parameters:
- Search by config_key substring or full key name
- Filter by value_type to retrieve only configuration entries of specific types
- Pagination with configurable page size and page number for efficient retrieval of large configuration sets
- Optional sorting by creation date or update date
- Optional filtering by version number to track configuration evolution

The operation returns paginated results including the total configuration count, current page number, and total pages available. Each returned configuration entry includes all metadata fields (key, value, type, description, version, timestamps) enabling complete configuration management and audit trail visibility.

Configuration values retrieved by this operation control system behavior - for example, 'max_todos_per_user' with value '10000' determines that each user can create up to 10,000 todos. The 'value_type' field indicates how to parse the config_value string (as integer 10000, boolean true/false, float 0.95, or string literal). This operation is essential for operational monitoring, configuration auditing, and system administration tasks.

When updating a configuration entry, the operation validates that the provided value matches the specified data type (string, integer, boolean, or float). The version number is automatically incremented each time an update occurs, enabling tracking of configuration evolution over time. The updated_at timestamp is set to the current time in UTC, recording when the change was made.

Security: Only authenticated administrators with system configuration privileges can perform this operation. The system prevents unauthorized users from modifying critical configuration settings. Configuration changes are logged for audit purposes with full details of what changed and when.

Validation: The provided config_value must be compatible with the specified value_type field. For example, a boolean type must receive 'true' or 'false'; an integer type must receive numeric string representations; float types must receive valid decimal strings. The operation returns HTTP 400 if the value does not match its type specification.

Audit Trail: Configuration changes are tracked through the incremented version field and updated_at timestamp. This enables operations teams to understand the history of configuration changes and potentially revert to previous values if needed.

operations.summary: Permanently delete a system configuration entry by configuration key
operations.description:
Permanently delete a system configuration entry by its unique configuration key. This operation removes the configuration completely from the system.

The system configuration table (todo_list_system_config) stores operational settings as key-value pairs. Deleting a configuration entry removes all information about that setting including the configuration key, value, type, description, version history, and timestamps.

Critical Warning: Deletion is permanent and irreversible. Once deleted, a configuration entry cannot be recovered. If a critical configuration is deleted (such as 'max_todos_per_user' or 'deployment_environment'), the system may revert to hardcoded default behavior or malfunction. Extreme caution should be exercised when deleting configuration entries.

Security: Only authenticated administrators with system configuration privileges can delete configuration entries. The system prevents unauthorized users from removing critical settings. Deletion attempts are logged for audit purposes with details of which configuration was deleted and when.

Audit Trail: The deletion is recorded in system audit logs including the administrator who performed the deletion, the configuration key that was deleted, the deletion timestamp, and the previous configuration values (for recovery/investigation purposes).

System Behavior: After deletion, if the system attempts to read the deleted configuration, it will either fail (if the configuration is mandatory) or fall back to hardcoded default values (if the configuration is optional). The application must handle missing configurations gracefully.

Recovery: There is no automatic recovery mechanism for deleted configurations. If a critical configuration is accidentally deleted, administrators must manually re-add the configuration through the create configuration API operation (POST /systemConfigurations) or restore from database backups.

Related Operations: Before deleting a configuration, administrators should first retrieve it with GET /systemConfigurations/{configKey} to confirm they are deleting the correct entry. For non-destructive inspection of all configurations, use PATCH /systemConfigurations to list all current settings.

ITodoListGuest.IAuthorized.description:
Authenticated guest user with valid JWT tokens for session access.

This DTO represents a guest user that has successfully authenticated and received valid JWT tokens. It is returned from both the guest join operation (initial registration) and the guest refresh operation (token renewal).

The guest user record is temporary and session-based. Guest accounts do not have persistent user profiles and are primarily identified by their session tokens. The id field serves as the session identifier for tracking purposes.

The token property contains the JWT tokens (access and refresh) that the guest must use for subsequent authenticated API requests.

id.description: Unique session identifier for the guest user. This UUID represents the current authenticated session and is used for session tracking and revocation purposes.

email.description: User's email address used for login and account recovery. Must be unique across all users. Stored in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

created_at.description: Timestamp when user account was created. Recorded in UTC timezone, ISO 8601 format.

ITodoListGuest.IRefresh.description:
Guest user refresh token request for renewing expired JWT access tokens.

This DTO is used when a guest user's access token has expired but their refresh token remains valid. The refresh operation validates the provided refresh token against the session and token management system to issue new JWT tokens.

The refresh token must be obtained from a previous guest join operation and must not have expired. The underlying session must remain active (not logged out) and within the absolute timeout window (30 days maximum).

Session activity is tracked and refreshed during this operation. If the guest's session has been inactive for more than 7 days since last activity, the refresh request will be rejected and the guest must re-register.

refresh_token.description: Valid refresh token from previous authentication response. This token is validated against the todo_list_sessions table to ensure the session is still active and the token has not expired. The token must be a valid JWT that was issued by a previous join or refresh operation.

ITodoListUser.ICreate.description:
User registration request for creating a new user account in the todo_list_users table.

This DTO captures the essential information needed to register a new user account. The email must be unique across all users and is validated for proper email format. Passwords are securely hashed using bcrypt (minimum cost factor 10) before storage; the plaintext password is never persisted in the database.

Upon successful user creation, a corresponding session is created in the todo_list_sessions table to represent the authenticated session context from the registration request. The session records client information (IP address, user agent) and establishes timeout parameters.

Session context fields (href, referrer, ip, user_agent) are required to capture the connection context for security and audit purposes. The href and referrer fields are mandatory (client must provide them), while the ip and user_agent fields are optional (server can extract from request headers if not provided, useful for server-side rendering scenarios).

JWT tokens are generated and returned upon successful registration, enabling immediate authenticated access to the API without requiring a separate login step.

email.description: User's email address for authentication and account identification. Must be unique across all users. Email addresses are stored in lowercase for case-insensitive matching during login. Must conform to RFC 5322 email format standards.

password.description: User's password in plaintext for verification and secure hashing. The password is never stored in plaintext; it is hashed using bcrypt (minimum cost factor 10) and stored in the password_hash field of the todo_list_users table. Minimum length requirement is 8 characters for security.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring. Optional - the server can extract the IP address from request headers if not provided. Useful in server-side rendering scenarios where the client IP cannot be directly determined.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) where the registration request originated. This is mandatory and must be provided by the client. Used for session context and security audit trails.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) indicating the origin of the registration request. This is mandatory and must be provided by the client. Can be an empty string for direct registration access. Used for session context and security tracking.

user_agent.description: Client user agent string for device and browser identification in session tracking. Optional - the server can extract from request headers if not provided. Useful in server-side rendering scenarios. Used for security monitoring and device tracking purposes.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:

Returned from login and token refresh endpoints. Provides complete user account information and authentication tokens in a single, unambiguous response structure.

Login credentials must be valid (email must exist, password must match) and the user account must be active (deleted_at must be null) for authentication to succeed. Invalid credentials or deleted accounts are rejected with a generic error message to prevent user enumeration attacks.

ITodoListUser.description:
Complete user profile information for authenticated users.

Represents the full account details of a user in the Todo List application. Contains identification information, contact details, authentication timestamps, and account lifecycle status. This type is used for profile retrieval and display operations where complete user information is required.

The password_hash field is intentionally excluded from this response type for security reasons - passwords are never exposed through the API, even in hashed form. All timestamp fields are recorded in UTC timezone using ISO 8601 format for consistency and interoperability.

The deleted_at field provides soft-delete support for audit trail preservation. When null, the account is active; when non-null, the account has been deleted but data is retained for historical purposes. The last_login_at field may be null for newly created accounts that have not yet logged in.

refresh_token.description: Valid refresh token obtained from login or previous token refresh. Used to generate a new short-lived access token without requiring password re-entry. Must not be expired or revoked.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Request body for refreshing an expired access token using a valid refresh token.

When access tokens expire, clients use this endpoint to obtain a new access token by providing their refresh token. The refresh token has a longer lifetime (typically 30 days) compared to access tokens (typically 15 minutes), enabling seamless user experience where background token refresh can occur without manual user intervention.

The refresh token is validated against expiration and the token blacklist (todo_list_token_blacklist) to ensure it has not been revoked through logout or password change operations.

email.description: Email address associated with the user account requesting password reset. Must match an existing active user account in the system.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetRequest.description: Request body for initiating a password reset flow. Contains the email address of the account requesting password recovery. A secure reset token will be generated and sent to this email address if the account exists and is active.

message.description:
Confirmation message indicating that a password reset link has been sent.

This message is generic and displays the same response whether the email exists in the system or not. This intentional consistency prevents email enumeration attacks where attackers could discover which email addresses are registered by observing different responses.

If the provided email address matches an active user account (deleted_at is null), a password reset token has been generated and sent to the registered email address. The reset token expires in 1 hour and can only be used once. If the email does not match any account or the account is deleted, no email is sent but the same success message is returned.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetRequestRespo.description:
Response body confirming that the password reset request was processed.

Returns a generic success message to prevent email enumeration attacks. The response is identical whether the requested email exists in the todo_list_users table or not, making it impossible for attackers to determine which email addresses are registered in the system.

When a matching active user account is found, a secure password reset token is automatically generated in the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table. This token is cryptographically random, time-limited (expires in 1 hour), and sent via email to the user's registered address. The token can only be consumed once - after successful password reset, the consumed_at field prevents reuse.

The reset token is hashed before storage to prevent exposure if the database is compromised. Users receive the token in an email link (e.g., /reset-password?token={token}) which they submit to the password reset confirmation endpoint along with their new password.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetConfirm.description:
Request payload for completing the password reset process.

This DTO is used when a user submits their password reset token (received via email link) along with their desired new password. The token must be the exact cryptographically secure random value provided in the password reset email link. The new password must meet security complexity requirements.

Both the token and new_password fields are required and validated on submission. The token is validated against the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table to ensure it exists, has not expired (created_at + 1 hour), and has not already been consumed (consumed_at is null). The new password is validated for complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters, containing at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character.

The plaintext password is never stored or logged. Upon successful validation, the new password is securely hashed using bcrypt (minimum cost factor 10) and stored in the todo_list_users.password_hash field. The reset token is marked as consumed, and all existing sessions and tokens for this user are revoked to force re-authentication with the new credentials.

token.description:
The password reset token received via email link.

This is the cryptographically secure random token value generated when the user requested password recovery via the password reset request endpoint. The token is included in the password reset link sent to the user's registered email address. It must match exactly with a token stored in the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table.

The token serves to verify that the user has received and accessed the password reset email. It acts as authorization to proceed with the password reset operation. The token is hashed in storage but provided in plaintext in the email link for user convenience.

new_password.description:
The new password for the user account.

Must meet security complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters in length, with at least one uppercase letter (A-Z), one lowercase letter (a-z), one number (0-9), and one special character (!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{};\':"|,.<>/?). These requirements prevent weak passwords and reduce vulnerability to brute-force attacks.

The password is validated on the backend before being processed. The plaintext password is never stored in the database or logged in application logs. Upon validation, it is immediately hashed using bcrypt with a minimum cost factor of 10, and only the hash is stored in the todo_list_users.password_hash field. This ensures that even if the database is compromised, plaintext passwords cannot be recovered.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetConfirmRespo.description:
Response confirming successful password reset completion.

Returned when the password reset process completes successfully. The response includes basic user information confirming which account was reset, and a success timestamp. The password hash is NOT included in the response - password hashes are never exposed in any API response.

After successful password reset, all existing sessions and tokens for this user are automatically invalidated as a security measure. The user must log in again with their new password via the login endpoint to establish a fresh authenticated session.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the user account whose password was reset.

This UUID identifies the user in the todo_list_users table. Used to confirm which account was affected by the password reset operation.

email.description:
Email address of the user account.

The email address registered with the user account, stored in lowercase in the todo_list_users table. Used for account recovery and communication. This confirms the password reset was applied to the correct account.

reset_completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset was successfully completed.

Recorded in UTC timezone, ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2025-11-18T09:03:30.084Z). Indicates when the new password became active in the system and when the todo_list_users.updated_at field was set.

sessions_invalidated.description:
Confirmation that all existing sessions for this user were invalidated.

Will always be true on successful password reset. All active sessions in the todo_list_sessions table for this user have been marked as expired (expired_at set to current time), and all active tokens have been added to the todo_list_token_blacklist. This forces the user to re-authenticate with their new password.

message.description:
Human-readable confirmation message.

Standard message indicating successful password reset. Example: 'Password has been successfully reset. Please log in with your new password.'.

ITodoListLogoutResponse.description:
Response confirming successful logout operation.

Returned by both single-device logout (POST /auth/user/logout) and global logout (POST /auth/user/logout-all-devices) operations. The response confirms that the user's session(s) have been terminated and token(s) have been invalidated.

For single-device logout, only the current session is affected. For global logout, all sessions across all devices are terminated. In both cases, the affected tokens are added to the todo_list_token_blacklist and become unusable for any further API requests.

success.description:
Indicates successful logout completion.

Will always be true in a success response. If logout fails, an error response is returned instead.

message.description:
Human-readable confirmation message.

For single-device logout: 'You have been logged out from this device.'
For global logout: 'You have been logged out from all devices. Please log in again.'

Informs the user of the logout scope and next steps.

sessions_affected.description:
Number of sessions that were terminated.

For single-device logout, this is always 1 (the current session).
For global logout, this is the total number of active sessions the user had before logout.

Used to inform users how many devices were affected by the logout operation.

logout_completed_at.description:
Timestamp when logout was completed.

Recorded in UTC timezone, ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2025-11-18T09:03:30.084Z). Indicates when the session termination and token invalidation took effect. Corresponds to when the todo_list_sessions.expired_at field was set for the affected sessions.

email.description: Updated email address for the user account. Must be lowercase and unique across all users to maintain the unique constraint. If provided, the system will validate the new email is not already in use by another account.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
Update request body for modifying authenticated user profile information.

Allows users to change their account details while maintaining security constraints and protecting system-managed fields. Only the email field can be updated through this operation. Password changes must be handled through a dedicated password change endpoint, not through this general profile update operation.

The created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, and last_login_at fields are system-managed and cannot be modified by users. The id field is immutable and cannot be changed. All provided fields are optional - only include fields that should be updated.

The system will automatically update the updated_at timestamp when changes are applied. Email updates must respect the unique constraint and cannot duplicate existing user emails in the system.

ITodoListSession.description:
User authentication session for managing multi-device login support.

Represents an authenticated session from a specific device or browser. Each user can have multiple concurrent sessions from different devices, and this table tracks each independent session separately. Sessions store device context (IP address, user agent) for security monitoring and enable multi-device login where a user can be logged in from multiple devices simultaneously with independent session management.

Sessions are created upon successful login and contain references to the user who owns them. Sessions can be invalidated through explicit logout (setting expired_at) or through token expiration/revocation. Each session maintains its own activity tracking and absolute maximum duration (30 days) to balance security with user convenience.

The last_activity_at field is updated on each authenticated request and enables implementing inactivity timeouts (7 days without activity). This provides security by preventing unauthorized use of dormant sessions while allowing active users to remain logged in indefinitely within the 30-day absolute limit.

id.description: Primary key uniquely identifying this authentication session. Used to reference and manage individual session records.

todo_list_user_id.description: Foreign key referencing the user who owns this session via the todo_list_users table. Links this authentication session to the specific user account (identified by todo_list_users.id) that initiated it. Corresponds to the Prisma schema column name todo_list_user_id.

ip_address.description: IP address from which the session was established. Used for session context tracking and security monitoring to detect unusual login patterns or suspicious authentication sources.

user_agent.description: HTTP User-Agent header from the device that established the session. Contains information about browser/device type. Used to display device information to users and detect suspicious sessions from unexpected device types.

created_at.description: Timestamp when session was created (login time). Recorded in UTC timezone, ISO 8601 format. Used for tracking session duration and age.

last_activity_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent API request using this session. Updated on each authenticated request. Used for implementing inactivity timeout (7 days) and session activity tracking.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when session was explicitly terminated (logout). Null while session is active. When set, all tokens associated with this session become invalid and cannot be reused.

absolute_timeout_at.description: Absolute maximum expiration time for this session (30 days from creation). Session must be terminated by this time regardless of activity. Used for enforcing maximum session duration per security requirements.

id.description: Primary key uniquely identifying this authentication session. Generated as UUID v4 upon session creation and immutable for the lifetime of the session.

todo_list_user_id.description: Foreign key referencing the user who owns this session. Links this session to the specific user account that initiated the login. Used to retrieve all sessions for a given user and to enforce user isolation when managing multi-device sessions.

ip_address.description: IP address from which the session was established. Captured at login time from the request. Displayed to users to help identify their own devices and detect unauthorized access from suspicious IP addresses. Useful for geographic or network-based security analysis.

user_agent.description: HTTP User-Agent header from the device. Contains browser and operating system information extracted from the request header. Displayed to users as readable device information (e.g., 'Chrome on Windows', 'Safari on iOS', 'Firefox on macOS'). Helps users identify and distinguish between their own devices.

created_at.description: Timestamp when session was created (login time). Recorded in UTC timezone using ISO 8601 format. Shows when the user logged in from this device. Used for determining session age and enforcing inactivity timeouts.

last_activity_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent API request using this session. Updated on each authenticated request. Shows last time the user was active on this device. Used for implementing inactivity timeout enforcement (7-day threshold) and tracking session usage patterns.

absolute_timeout_at.description: Absolute maximum expiration time for this session (30 days from creation). Represents a hard deadline for session validity regardless of activity. Session must be terminated by this time even if continuously active. Used for enforcing maximum session duration per security requirements and preventing indefinitely long-lived sessions.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when session was explicitly terminated (logout). Null for active sessions indicating the session is still valid and can be used for API requests. Non-null value indicates the session has been explicitly revoked (user logged out) and all associated tokens become invalid. When set, the session cannot be used for subsequent authentication.

ITodoListSession.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of an authentication session for list views and device management.

Represents a single authenticated session from a specific device or browser. Includes essential session metadata displayed to users when viewing their active devices and login history. Shows login IP address and device information (User-Agent), along with session creation and last activity timestamps for activity tracking.

The expired_at field indicates whether the session is active (null) or has been terminated (non-null timestamp). The absolute_timeout_at field shows the hard deadline for this session's validity regardless of activity level.

Optimized for efficient display in session management interfaces where users view their active devices, identify unusual login activity, and can revoke sessions from other devices for enhanced account security. Each session maintains independent token management and can be terminated independently without affecting other concurrent sessions.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Starts at 1. Determines which page of results to return based on the limit parameter. Required for paginated queries.

limit.description: Number of sessions to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 10 if not specified. Controls pagination granularity for session lists and prevents unbounded result sets.

search.description: Optional search term to filter sessions by device identification. Can search by IP address using exact or partial matching, or by user agent partial matching for finding specific devices. Enables users to quickly locate sessions from particular devices or IP ranges. When omitted, all sessions are included in results without search filtering.

status.description: Filter sessions by operational status. 'active' returns only sessions with null expired_at (currently logged in and usable). 'expired' returns only sessions with non-null expired_at (terminated and no longer usable). Null or omitted returns all sessions regardless of status. Essential for distinguishing between active login sessions and revoked/logged-out sessions.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. 'created_at' sorts by session creation time (login timestamp). 'last_activity_at' sorts by most recent API request time. 'ip_address' sorts alphabetically by IP address for device identification. Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified, showing oldest sessions first.

order.description: Sort direction for results. 'asc' for ascending order (oldest/smallest first). 'desc' for descending order (newest/largest first). Defaults to 'desc' (most recent first) if not specified, showing recently created or active sessions at the top of the list.

created_after.description: Optional filter for sessions created after this ISO 8601 timestamp (inclusive). Used for finding recently created sessions within a specific time range. Helps identify new login activity. When omitted, no lower bound is applied to creation time.

created_before.description: Optional filter for sessions created before this ISO 8601 timestamp (inclusive). Used for finding older sessions within a specific time range. Helps identify sessions from particular periods or before a specific date. When omitted, no upper bound is applied to creation time.

last_activity_after.description: Optional filter for sessions with last activity after this ISO 8601 timestamp (inclusive). Used for finding recently active sessions, typically within the past N days. Helps identify sessions that have been actively used. When omitted, no lower bound is applied to last activity time.

ITodoListSession.IRequest.description:
Search criteria, filtering options, and pagination parameters for retrieving and filtering user authentication sessions.

Supports advanced filtering by session status (active vs expired/revoked), creation date ranges, and last activity time ranges. Enables sorting by multiple attributes (creation date, last activity timestamp, IP address) with configurable sort direction (ascending or descending).

Includes pagination parameters for managing large session lists efficiently. All filter and search parameters are optional and can be combined to create complex search queries. For example, users can find all active sessions from a specific IP range created within the past 7 days.

Used by the session list search endpoint to provide users with flexible session filtering, browsing, and management capabilities for monitoring their multi-device login activity and revoking unauthorized sessions.

ITodoListUser.ITokenVerification.description:
Token verification result containing validity status, user information, and token metadata.

This schema represents the response from a token verification operation that validates the authenticity, expiration, revocation status, and account validity of a user's JWT authentication token.

The verification process checks: (1) token signature validity, (2) expiration time against current time, (3) revocation status against the todo_list_token_blacklist table, and (4) user account active status (deleted_at is null in todo_list_users table).

This response enables clients to preemptively detect expired or revoked tokens before attempting other API calls, facilitating graceful token refresh or re-authentication flows in multi-device authentication scenarios.

is_valid.description: Indicates whether the JWT token is currently valid and can be used for authenticated requests. True means the token has valid signature, has not expired, has not been revoked, and the associated user account is still active. False indicates the token has failed one or more validation checks and should not be used for further API calls.

user_id.description: The unique identifier of the user associated with this token, extracted from the token's 'sub' (subject) claim. This ID corresponds to a record in the todo_list_users table.

token_jti.description: The unique JWT ID (jti claim) identifying this specific token instance. This identifier is used to track token revocation in the todo_list_token_blacklist table when users logout or change passwords.

issued_at.description: The timestamp when this JWT token was originally issued, extracted from the 'iat' (issued at) claim. Used to calculate token age and validate against system time drift.

expires_at.description: The timestamp when this JWT token will expire and become invalid, extracted from the 'exp' (expiration time) claim. After this time, the token cannot be used for authenticated requests and must be refreshed.

remaining_lifetime_seconds.description: The number of seconds remaining before this token expires. Calculated as (expires_at - current_time). Zero or negative values indicate the token has already expired.

is_revoked.description: Indicates whether this specific token has been explicitly revoked (blacklisted) in the todo_list_token_blacklist table. Tokens are revoked when users logout or change their passwords. Even if not expired, revoked tokens cannot be used for authenticated requests.

user_account_active.description: Indicates whether the user account associated with this token is still active and not deleted. Checked by verifying the user's deleted_at field is null in the todo_list_users table. If false, the token cannot be used even if otherwise valid.

failure_reason.description: If is_valid is false, this field provides a human-readable explanation of why the token failed verification. Possible values include: 'signature_invalid', 'token_expired', 'token_revoked', 'user_account_deleted', or other specific failure reasons. If is_valid is true, this field is null.

ITodoListAuth.IGuestLogoutResponse.description:
Confirmation message that guest session has been successfully terminated.

This schema represents the response from a guest logout operation that terminates an unauthenticated guest user session. Unlike authenticated user logout which revokes JWT tokens in the todo_list_token_blacklist table, guest logout performs lightweight session cleanup appropriate for transient, unauthenticated users.

Guest users have limited functionality and no persistent account in the todo_list_users table. Their sessions are temporary and can be safely terminated without complex revocation procedures. This response confirms the guest session has been cleared and any guest-specific session identifiers or local state should be considered invalid.

success.description: Indicates whether the guest session was successfully terminated. True means the guest logout operation completed successfully and the guest session is now invalid. False indicates the logout operation failed and the guest session may still be active.

message.description: A human-readable confirmation message explaining the result of the guest logout operation. Example messages: 'Guest session successfully terminated' or 'Thank you for using the application'.

title.description: Todo task title. Required field describing what the todo is about. Must be non-empty after trimming whitespace. Length between 1-255 characters.

description.description: Optional detailed description of the todo task. Provides additional context or notes about what needs to be done. Length 0-5000 characters. Null or omitted when not provided.

completed.description: Completion status of the todo. True indicates the todo is marked complete and done. False indicates the todo is pending or incomplete. Initialized to false when created. Can be toggled by the user at any time.

priority.description: Priority level for this todo task. One of: "low", "medium", or "high". Defaults to "medium" if not specified during creation. Optional field.

due_date.description: Optional due date for completing this todo. Must be today or in the future (cannot be in the past). Represented in ISO 8601 format. Null when not set.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when this todo was marked as complete. Recorded in UTC timezone using ISO 8601 format when completion status changes to true. Automatically cleared when marked incomplete. Null while todo is still pending.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this todo was created. System-generated and immutable, recorded in UTC timezone. Used for sorting by newest/oldest first and audit trail purposes.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this todo. Updated whenever any field changes including title, description, completion status, priority, or due date. Tracks modification history in UTC timezone.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Complete todo item representation for detailed retrieval operations.

Represents a personal todo task owned by an authenticated user with all available fields including title, description, priority, and due date information. Contains full modification history through timestamps.

Each todo is exclusively owned by the authenticated user who created it. The todo includes completion tracking with optional completion timestamp, priority classification, and optional due date for task scheduling.

Used in single-item retrieval operations (GET /todos/:id) to provide complete information about a specific todo without requiring additional API calls.

title.description: Todo task title (required). What the todo is about. Must be non-empty after trimming whitespace.

description.description: Optional detailed description of the todo task. Additional context or notes. Can be null or omitted.

priority.description: Priority level for this todo. One of: "low", "medium", "high". Defaults to "medium" if not specified.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new todo item.

Accepts the essential fields needed to create a todo: title (required), description (optional), priority level (optional, defaults to medium), and due date (optional, must not be in past).

The authenticated user's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT token - do not include user_id or authentication fields in the request. The system automatically sets creation timestamp and completion status (false by default).

Used in POST /todos operations to create new todo items owned by the authenticated user.

id.description: Unique identifier for this todo item. System-generated UUID used to reference the todo in all subsequent API operations including updates, deletions, and detailed retrievals.

title.description: Todo task title providing brief, human-readable description of what needs to be done. Must be between 1-255 characters after whitespace trimming. Cannot be empty or contain only whitespace.

completed.description: Completion status of the todo item. True indicates the task has been marked as complete and done; false indicates the task is pending or incomplete. Users can toggle this status at any time, and the system records the completion timestamp when transitioning from incomplete to complete.

priority.description: Priority level classification for organizing and prioritizing todos. One of: low, medium, or high. Defaults to medium when not specified. Helps users focus on important tasks and can be used for sorting and filtering. Null when not explicitly set.

due_date.description: Optional target date and time for completing this todo. Provided in ISO 8601 format when specified. Must be today or in the future; past dates are not permitted to ensure todos reference realistic deadlines. Null when not set, indicating no specific deadline.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:

Includes essential fields needed to display todos in list views: unique identifier, title, completion status, priority level, and timestamps for sorting and change tracking. Excludes large text fields like full description for efficient data transfer and rapid rendering of paginated results.

Used in list retrieval operations (PATCH /todoList/user/todos) with pagination support to efficiently display multiple todos without unnecessary data overhead while preserving key metadata for user decisions.
